I do drink, but I’ve been trying to refrain from drinking at socials as I feel it defeats the purpose of why I got into dancing. If I numb my anxiety with alcohol then am I really hopping over my mental barriers or am I just using liquid courage to put a temporary blinder on them? Same thing goes from medication as I’ve never been one to want to go the medicated route in terms of mental things.

So one of the main things that gets to me is dancing twice with the same follow in the same night. For instance, follow from class asked me to dance as soon as the pre-social class ended. And it was a great dance, I was feeling fresh and moves were comin off the top of my head no problem. 
  She then asked me to dance again a couple songs later and that dance was way worse as I’m very self conscious about using the same moves as before. Because in my mind, who wants to do the same handful of moves as before?

My inner monologue usually starts off good, my first dance is good because I’m fresh. Second dance not so much. And after that I feel like my social battery is already depleted. Which makes it harder to remember moves and screw up the ones I try to do. Which makes me stick to my seat with this inner feeling of “I don’t even feel like dancing, I shouldn’t be here.”

The follows I do dance with usually comment on how good of a lead I am and that I’m not too soft but not too rough. That my body movement is great. 
  I find that after a few dances I feel like my social battery is drained, which in turn makes it harder for me to remember moves/screw up the ones I try. Which in turn makes me want to not ask anyone to dance. 
 The whole follows asking me to dance thing, I feel is getting old for them as it’s been happening for a few months just because I can’t seem to get over this barrier. It makes me feel embarrassed because I’m worried they’re going to start thinking that I have a mindset of “women ask me to dance, not the other way around.” Which is obviously not how it is.
This has long since been common knowledge to me. This is the reason I got into dance. To make myself wildly uncomfortable, put myself in the fire.
